- `annotationsStatus` — string _(enum: `AVAILABLE`, `UNAVAILABLE`)_
- `annotationsByKey` — AnnotationsMap — The newest annotation per `AnnotationKey`: the current value of everything the conversation tracks, without reading the history. Keyed annotations only — a one-off annotation appears solely in `annotations`.
  - _map of_ `Annotation`
    - `id` — string **(required)** — Identity of this emission. Annotations are applied once per id: re-sending one already recorded on the conversation is ignored.
    - `time` — number **(required)**
    - `key` — string — Identity of the value, when the annotation is one reading of something that changes over the conversation. See AnnotationKey. _(pattern=^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]*$; maxLen=100)_
    - `payload` — union **(required)**
      - _oneOf_ — exactly one of:
        - **`tag`**
          - _(nesting depth limit — inline object, see the parent schema in the Schemas appendix)_
        - **`text`**
          - _(nesting depth limit — inline object, see the parent schema in the Schemas appendix)_
        - **`variables`**
          - _(nesting depth limit — inline object, see the parent schema in the Schemas appendix)_
        - **`result`**
          - _(nesting depth limit — inline object, see the parent schema in the Schemas appendix)_
        - **`metric`**
          - _(nesting depth limit — inline object, see the parent schema in the Schemas appendix)_
    - `source` — AnnotationSource **(required)** — Producer of an annotation. Generic identifiers allow callers to attach context such as tool id/name, user id/name, etc., without constraining the source type to a fixed shape.
      - `type` — string **(required)** _(enum: `chatbot`, `voicebot`, `user`, `system`, `copilot`)_
      - `id` — string — Stable identifier of the producer (e.g. tool id, user id, copilot session id).
      - `name` — string — Human-readable name of the producer (e.g. tool name, user display name).
- `type` — object **(required)**

Classound emits QUEUED, SENT, DELIVERED (a provider read report is sent as DELIVERED), DELETED, 24H_CHANNEL_CLOSED and FAILED. ERROR and READ are not emitted by Classound; do not remove them while consumers may still receive them. _(enum: `QUEUED`, `SENT`, `DELIVERED`, `FAILED`, `ERROR`, `READ`, `DELETED`, `24H_CHANNEL_CLOSED`)_

      - `type` — object **(required)**
      - `data` — MessengerInboundConsumeEventData **(required)**
        - `id` — string **(required)** — The supplier's message id, kept whole: it carries no part of ours. Empty on an event delivery that carries no reference, which CM.com's generic envelope allows: the producer sends the key with an empty value rather than inventing an id, so no length is claimed here
        - `from` — string **(required)** — The sender's Page Scoped ID, up to 17 decimal digits. Not a phone number and never normalised _(minLen=4)_
        - `to` — string **(required)** — The Facebook Page ID the message arrived on. Not a phone number and never normalised _(minLen=4)_
        - `message` — string **(required)** — The text, or the pressed button's own label on a quick reply. Empty on an opt-in or a media only message
        - `channel` — string **(required)** — Always "messenger": the channel stated outright rather than inferred from type

          - _(nesting depth limit — see `MessengerAccount` in the Schemas appendix)_
        - `contact` — MessengerContact

        - `window` — MessengerWindow
          - _(nesting depth limit — see `MessengerWindow` in the Schemas appendix)_

          - _array of_ `string`

  - **`messengerStatus`**
    - `messengerStatus` — MessengerStatusConsumeEvent **(required)** — A delivery report for a Messenger message an agent sent, put on the stream by classound from the CM.com status callback
      - `pbx` — string **(required)**
      - `company` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
      - `time` — number **(required)** — Epoch MILLIseconds. Long rather than Integer because a millisecond timestamp outgrew the 32 bit range 25 days after 1970: every producer that mixes in this base, SMS and Messenger, has always sent 13 digits
      - `type` — object **(required)**
      - `data` — MessengerStatusConsumeEventData **(required)** — Four differences from the WhatsApp status event this shape was copied from, all four deliberate. Two members are absent. `parts`, because a Messenger message is never segmented the way an SMS is: classound splits a reply into one Messenger message per file plus one for the text, each with its own reference and its own report of its own, so the count a consumer needs is the number of references the send returned and not a number carried on any one report. `batchId`, because nothing broadcasts on this channel: it exists on the WhatsApp event to group the per-recipient statuses of an a2s broadcast, and a Messenger send has one recipient and no batch. Two members are present but declared differently. `reason` is optional here and @required on WhatsApp, because CM.com sends an empty description on a Messenger report often enough that the producer omits the member rather than sending an empty string, and a consumer that only ever reads it on a failure loses nothing. `channel` is an untyped @required String here, where the SMS event has the typed SmsChannelType and the WhatsApp event a `= "whatsapp"` default: this channel has exactly one value, so an enum of one member would carry nothing an enum can carry, and the value is stated by the producer on every event rather than defaulted, so that a consumer never has to decide whether an absent member means messenger or means a producer that forgot
        - `id` — string **(required)** — The reference the send returned in messageIds and MDR holds as supplier_message_id, messenger_<page id>_<uuid4 hex>. A status is matched to the chat message it reports on by this value alone
        - `from` — string **(required)** — The Facebook Page ID the message was sent from, read out of the reference. Not a phone number and never normalised _(minLen=4)_
        - `to` — string **(required)** — The recipient's Page Scoped ID as CM.com reports it. Not a phone number and never normalised _(minLen=4)_
        - `status` — string **(required)** — The final states CM.com reports for a Messenger message, exactly as the producer maps the supplier codes: 1 and 3 are FAILED, 2 is DELIVERED, 4 is READ. Code 0, accepted by the operator, is intermediate and is dropped before the stream, so there is no member for it. The failure is named FAILED and not ERROR, which is what the sibling WhatsApp channel enum calls the same thing: these are the supplier's reports and not a message state, and CM.com's own word for a report of this kind is failed. The consumers translate, kite to MessageMessengerStatus.ERROR and rnc to the red indicator, and the translation is one line in each _(enum: `DELIVERED`, `READ`, `FAILED`)_
        - `reason` — string — CM.com's errorDescription, verbatim. Present on a failure; CM.com also sends one on a success ('Delivered')
        - `channel` — string **(required)** — Always "messenger": the channel stated outright rather than inferred from type
  - **`rcsInbound`**

    - `rcsStatus` — RcsStatusConsumeEvent **(required)** — A delivery report for an RCS message an x-bees user sent, put on the stream by classound from the CM.com status callback
      - `pbx` — string **(required)**
      - `company` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
      - `time` — number **(required)** — Epoch MILLIseconds. Long rather than Integer because a millisecond timestamp outgrew the 32 bit range 25 days after 1970: every producer that mixes in this base, SMS and Messenger, has always sent 13 digits
      - `type` — object **(required)**
      - `data` — RcsStatusConsumeEventData **(required)** — Shaped as the Messenger status event, with the same four differences from the WhatsApp one: no `parts`, because each file and the text go out as messages of their own with a reference each; no `batchId`, because nothing broadcasts on this channel; `reason` optional, because CM.com often sends it empty; `channel` an untyped @required String, because the channel has one value and the producer states it on every event
        - `id` — string **(required)** — The reference the send returned in messageIds, rcs_<brand id>_<uuid4 hex>. A status is matched to the chat message it reports on by this value alone

    - **`messengerStatus`**
      - `messengerStatus` — MessengerStatusConsumeEvent **(required)** — A delivery report for a Messenger message an agent sent, put on the stream by classound from the CM.com status callback
        - `pbx` — string **(required)**
        - `company` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
        - `time` — number **(required)** — Epoch MILLIseconds. Long rather than Integer because a millisecond timestamp outgrew the 32 bit range 25 days after 1970: every producer that mixes in this base, SMS and Messenger, has always sent 13 digits
        - `type` — object **(required)**
          - _(nesting depth limit — inline object, see the parent schema in the Schemas appendix)_
        - `data` — MessengerStatusConsumeEventData **(required)** — Four differences from the WhatsApp status event this shape was copied from, all four deliberate. Two members are absent. `parts`, because a Messenger message is never segmented the way an SMS is: classound splits a reply into one Messenger message per file plus one for the text, each with its own reference and its own report of its own, so the count a consumer needs is the number of references the send returned and not a number carried on any one report. `batchId`, because nothing broadcasts on this channel: it exists on the WhatsApp event to group the per-recipient statuses of an a2s broadcast, and a Messenger send has one recipient and no batch. Two members are present but declared differently. `reason` is optional here and @required on WhatsApp, because CM.com sends an empty description on a Messenger report often enough that the producer omits the member rather than sending an empty string, and a consumer that only ever reads it on a failure loses nothing. `channel` is an untyped @required String here, where the SMS event has the typed SmsChannelType and the WhatsApp event a `= "whatsapp"` default: this channel has exactly one value, so an enum of one member would carry nothing an enum can carry, and the value is stated by the producer on every event rather than defaulted, so that a consumer never has to decide whether an absent member means messenger or means a producer that forgot
          - _(nesting depth limit — see `MessengerStatusConsumeEventData` in the Schemas appendix)_
    - **`rcsInbound`**
      - `rcsInbound` — RcsInboundConsumeEvent **(required)** — An inbound RCS message, put on the stream by classound
        - `pbx` — string **(required)**
        - `company` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
        - `time` — number **(required)** — Epoch MILLIseconds. Long rather than Integer because a millisecond timestamp outgrew the 32 bit range 25 days after 1970: every producer that mixes in this base, SMS and Messenger, has always sent 13 digits
        - `type` — object **(required)**
          - _(nesting depth limit — inline object, see the parent schema in the Schemas appendix)_
        - `data` — RcsInboundConsumeEventData **(required)**
          - _(nesting depth limit — see `RcsInboundConsumeEventData` in the Schemas appendix)_
    - **`rcsStatus`**
      - `rcsStatus` — RcsStatusConsumeEvent **(required)** — A delivery report for an RCS message an x-bees user sent, put on the stream by classound from the CM.com status callback
        - `pbx` — string **(required)**
        - `company` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
        - `time` — number **(required)** — Epoch MILLIseconds. Long rather than Integer because a millisecond timestamp outgrew the 32 bit range 25 days after 1970: every producer that mixes in this base, SMS and Messenger, has always sent 13 digits
        - `type` — object **(required)**
          - _(nesting depth limit — inline object, see the parent schema in the Schemas appendix)_
        - `data` — RcsStatusConsumeEventData **(required)** — Shaped as the Messenger status event, with the same four differences from the WhatsApp one: no `parts`, because each file and the text go out as messages of their own with a reference each; no `batchId`, because nothing broadcasts on this channel; `reason` optional, because CM.com often sends it empty; `channel` an untyped @required String, because the channel has one value and the producer states it on every event

- `SmsInboundEvent` — SmsInboundEvent
  - `pbx` — string **(required)**
  - `company` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
  - `time` — number **(required)** — Epoch MILLIseconds. Long rather than Integer because a millisecond timestamp outgrew the 32 bit range 25 days after 1970: every producer that mixes in this base, SMS and Messenger, has always sent 13 digits
  - `type` — object **(required)**
  - `data` — SmsInboundConsumeEventData **(required)**
    - `id` — string **(required)** — A unique ID of the SMS message (example fb0ee129-f98f-4d7f-af1e-32b657aa3a56) _(minLen=3)_
    - `from` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3)_
    - `to` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3)_
    - `message` — string **(required)** _(minLen=1)_
    - `media` — array
      - _array of_ `string`
- `SmsStatusEvent` — SmsStatusEvent
  - `pbx` — string **(required)**
  - `company` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
  - `time` — number **(required)** — Epoch MILLIseconds. Long rather than Integer because a millisecond timestamp outgrew the 32 bit range 25 days after 1970: every producer that mixes in this base, SMS and Messenger, has always sent 13 digits
  - `type` — object **(required)**
  - `data` — SmsStatusConsumeEventData **(required)**
    - `id` — string **(required)**
    - `from` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3)_
    - `to` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3)_
    - `status` — string **(required)** _(enum: `sent`, `delivered`, `trying`, `error`)_
    - `reason` — string — Failure reason from supplier (example 'inactive-campaign'
    - `channel` — string **(required)** _(enum: `1-way-sms`, `2-way-sms`)_
    - `parts` — number **(required)**
- `WhatsAppInboundEvent` — WhatsAppInboundEvent
  - `pbx` — string **(required)**
  - `company` — string **(required)**
  - `time` — number **(required)** _(format=double)_
  - `type` — object **(required)**
  - `data` — WhatsAppInboundEventData **(required)**
    - `from` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3)_
    - `to` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3)_
    - `id` — string **(required)** — A unique ID of the WhatsApp message
    - `message` — string **(required)**
    - `contact` — WhatsAppContact
      - `name` — string — The sender's WhatsApp profile name as the supplier reports it. Best effort: the whole object is omitted when it is unknown
    - `media` — array
      - _array of_ `string`
    - `quoteMessageId` — string
- `WhatsAppStatusEvent` — WhatsAppStatusEvent
  - `pbx` — string **(required)**
  - `company` — string **(required)**
  - `time` — number **(required)** _(format=double)_
  - `type` — object **(required)**
  - `data` — WhatsAppStatusEventData **(required)**
    - `from` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3)_
    - `to` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3)_
    - `id` — string **(required)**
    - `status` — string **(required)** — Delivery status of an outbound WhatsApp message in a WHATSAPP.STATUS event. Classound emits QUEUED, SENT, DELIVERED (a provider read report is sent as DELIVERED), DELETED, 24H_CHANNEL_CLOSED and FAILED. ERROR and READ are not emitted by Classound; do not remove them while consumers may still receive them. _(enum: `QUEUED`, `SENT`, `DELIVERED`, `FAILED`, `ERROR`, `READ`, `DELETED`, `24H_CHANNEL_CLOSED`)_
    - `reason` — string **(required)**
    - `channel` — string _(default=whatsapp)_
    - `parts` — number
    - `batchId` — string — Broadcast batch id from the a2s send response; correlates the status back to the originating API call. Absent for non-broadcast messages.
- `MessengerInboundEvent` — MessengerInboundEvent
  - `pbx` — string **(required)**
  - `company` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
  - `time` — number **(required)** — Epoch MILLIseconds. Long rather than Integer because a millisecond timestamp outgrew the 32 bit range 25 days after 1970: every producer that mixes in this base, SMS and Messenger, has always sent 13 digits
  - `type` — object **(required)**
  - `data` — MessengerInboundConsumeEventData **(required)**
    - `id` — string **(required)** — The supplier's message id, kept whole: it carries no part of ours. Empty on an event delivery that carries no reference, which CM.com's generic envelope allows: the producer sends the key with an empty value rather than inventing an id, so no length is claimed here
    - `from` — string **(required)** — The sender's Page Scoped ID, up to 17 decimal digits. Not a phone number and never normalised _(minLen=4)_
    - `to` — string **(required)** — The Facebook Page ID the message arrived on. Not a phone number and never normalised _(minLen=4)_
    - `message` — string **(required)** — The text, or the pressed button's own label on a quick reply. Empty on an opt-in or a media only message
    - `channel` — string **(required)** — Always "messenger": the channel stated outright rather than inferred from type
    - `account` — MessengerAccount **(required)**
      - `id` — string **(required)** — The Facebook Page ID the message arrived on, the same value as data.to, and constrained the same way so that one value is not declared under two grammars in one event _(minLen=4)_
      - `name` — string — The page's display name, so the agent knows who they are answering as
    - `contact` — MessengerContact
      - `name` — string — The sender's display name as the supplier reports it. Best effort: the whole object is omitted when it is unknown
    - `postback` — string — Our own payload behind a quick reply, absent on a typed message
    - `window` — MessengerWindow
      - `freeFormUntil` — number **(required)** — Epoch seconds until which a free-form reply still reaches the person (Meta's 24 hour window)
      - `agentReplyUntil` — number **(required)** — Epoch seconds until which a reply tagged HUMAN_AGENT still reaches the person. 0 when no such window is open
    - `media` — array
      - _array of_ `string`
    - `event` — MessengerDeliveryEvent — Present when the delivery is not a message at all, for example a Marketing Messages opt-in. The type is reported whatever it is, including one the supplier has not documented
      - `type` — string **(required)**
      - `notificationToken` — string — The Marketing Messages notification token: the address every later marketing message to this person is sent to
      - `tokenExpiry` — string
- `MessengerStatusEvent` — MessengerStatusEvent
  - `pbx` — string **(required)**
  - `company` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
  - `time` — number **(required)** — Epoch MILLIseconds. Long rather than Integer because a millisecond timestamp outgrew the 32 bit range 25 days after 1970: every producer that mixes in this base, SMS and Messenger, has always sent 13 digits
  - `type` — object **(required)**
  - `data` — MessengerStatusConsumeEventData **(required)** — Four differences from the WhatsApp status event this shape was copied from, all four deliberate. Two members are absent. `parts`, because a Messenger message is never segmented the way an SMS is: classound splits a reply into one Messenger message per file plus one for the text, each with its own reference and its own report of its own, so the count a consumer needs is the number of references the send returned and not a number carried on any one report. `batchId`, because nothing broadcasts on this channel: it exists on the WhatsApp event to group the per-recipient statuses of an a2s broadcast, and a Messenger send has one recipient and no batch. Two members are present but declared differently. `reason` is optional here and @required on WhatsApp, because CM.com sends an empty description on a Messenger report often enough that the producer omits the member rather than sending an empty string, and a consumer that only ever reads it on a failure loses nothing. `channel` is an untyped @required String here, where the SMS event has the typed SmsChannelType and the WhatsApp event a `= "whatsapp"` default: this channel has exactly one value, so an enum of one member would carry nothing an enum can carry, and the value is stated by the producer on every event rather than defaulted, so that a consumer never has to decide whether an absent member means messenger or means a producer that forgot
    - `id` — string **(required)** — The reference the send returned in messageIds and MDR holds as supplier_message_id, messenger_<page id>_<uuid4 hex>. A status is matched to the chat message it reports on by this value alone
    - `from` — string **(required)** — The Facebook Page ID the message was sent from, read out of the reference. Not a phone number and never normalised _(minLen=4)_
    - `to` — string **(required)** — The recipient's Page Scoped ID as CM.com reports it. Not a phone number and never normalised _(minLen=4)_
    - `status` — string **(required)** — The final states CM.com reports for a Messenger message, exactly as the producer maps the supplier codes: 1 and 3 are FAILED, 2 is DELIVERED, 4 is READ. Code 0, accepted by the operator, is intermediate and is dropped before the stream, so there is no member for it. The failure is named FAILED and not ERROR, which is what the sibling WhatsApp channel enum calls the same thing: these are the supplier's reports and not a message state, and CM.com's own word for a report of this kind is failed. The consumers translate, kite to MessageMessengerStatus.ERROR and rnc to the red indicator, and the translation is one line in each _(enum: `DELIVERED`, `READ`, `FAILED`)_
    - `reason` — string — CM.com's errorDescription, verbatim. Present on a failure; CM.com also sends one on a success ('Delivered')
    - `channel` — string **(required)** — Always "messenger": the channel stated outright rather than inferred from type
- `RcsInboundEvent` — RcsInboundEvent
  - `pbx` — string **(required)**
  - `company` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
  - `time` — number **(required)** — Epoch MILLIseconds. Long rather than Integer because a millisecond timestamp outgrew the 32 bit range 25 days after 1970: every producer that mixes in this base, SMS and Messenger, has always sent 13 digits
  - `type` — object **(required)**
  - `data` — RcsInboundConsumeEventData **(required)**
    - `id` — string **(required)** — The supplier's message id. Empty on an event delivery that carries no reference: the producer sends the key with an empty value rather than inventing an id, so no length is claimed here
    - `from` — string **(required)** — The sender's phone number as CM.com reports it, with a leading 00 rewritten to +. Otherwise passed through unchecked, so a consumer does not assume E.164 _(minLen=4)_
    - `to` — string **(required)** — The brand id the message arrived on. Not a phone number and never normalised _(minLen=1)_
    - `message` — string **(required)** — The text, or the pressed button's own label on a suggested reply. Empty on a media only message
    - `channel` — string **(required)** — Always "rcs": the channel stated outright rather than inferred from type
    - `account` — RcsAccount **(required)**
      - `id` — string **(required)** — The brand id the message arrived on, the same value as data.to _(minLen=1)_
    - `contact` — RcsContact
      - `name` — string — The sender's display name as the supplier reports it. Best effort: the whole object is omitted when it is unknown
    - `postback` — string — Our own payload behind a suggested reply, absent on a typed message
    - `media` — array
      - _array of_ `string`
    - `event` — RcsDeliveryEvent — Present when the delivery is not a message at all, for example a suggestion button press that CM.com reports as an event. The type is reported whatever it is, including one the supplier has not documented, so a consumer ignores a type it does not know
      - `type` — string **(required)**
- `RcsStatusEvent` — RcsStatusEvent
  - `pbx` — string **(required)**
  - `company` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
  - `time` — number **(required)** — Epoch MILLIseconds. Long rather than Integer because a millisecond timestamp outgrew the 32 bit range 25 days after 1970: every producer that mixes in this base, SMS and Messenger, has always sent 13 digits
  - `type` — object **(required)**
  - `data` — RcsStatusConsumeEventData **(required)** — Shaped as the Messenger status event, with the same four differences from the WhatsApp one: no `parts`, because each file and the text go out as messages of their own with a reference each; no `batchId`, because nothing broadcasts on this channel; `reason` optional, because CM.com often sends it empty; `channel` an untyped @required String, because the channel has one value and the producer states it on every event
    - `id` — string **(required)** — The reference the send returned in messageIds, rcs_<brand id>_<uuid4 hex>. A status is matched to the chat message it reports on by this value alone
    - `from` — string **(required)** — The brand id the message was sent from, read out of the reference. Not a phone number and never normalised _(minLen=1)_
    - `to` — string **(required)** — The recipient's phone number in E.164 as CM.com reports it, or "unknown" when the report carries none
    - `status` — string **(required)** — The final states CM.com reports for an RCS message, mapped as on Messenger: 1 and 3 are FAILED, 2 is DELIVERED, 4 is READ. Code 0 is intermediate and is dropped before the stream _(enum: `DELIVERED`, `READ`, `FAILED`)_
    - `reason` — string — CM.com's errorDescription, verbatim. Omitted when CM.com sends it empty
    - `channel` — string **(required)** — Always "rcs": the channel stated outright rather than inferred from type
- `WebsocketAuthorizeAction` — WebsocketAuthorizeAction
  - `action` — object **(required)**
  - `token` — string **(required)**
- `WebsocketSubscribeAction` — WebsocketSubscribeAction
  - `action` — object **(required)**
  - `topic` — string **(required)** _(enum: `conversations`, `transcriptions`, `presence`, `services`)_
  - `filter` — array
    - _array of_ `any`
  - `state` — boolean
  - `version` — string
  - `stats` — boolean — Services topic only. Opt in to stats: the subscribe snapshot then carries stats and the connection receives service_stats_update events. Stats are also enabled by any of periodMinutes, periodStartAt, periodStart, utcOffsetMinutes or serviceLevelSeconds. Without any of them the subscription gets service and call events only. Ignored for other topics.
  - `buckets` — boolean — Services topic only. Set to true to also get stats.buckets (the stats window as a time series, for trend charts) in the subscribe snapshot and in every service_stats_update. Implies stats. Defaults to false: the series is the largest part of the stats, so it is sent only to the subscriptions that ask for it.
  - `periodMinutes` — number — Services topic only. Rolling lookback window in minutes: omit or 15 for the current 15-minute UTC bucket; 30, 45 or 60 for the last 30, 45 or 60 minutes, read from 15-minute UTC buckets (kept for the last hour only), so the oldest bucket is counted whole and the covered span reported in periodSeconds is up to 15 minutes more. For longer windows use periodStartAt or periodStart. Cannot be combined with periodStartAt or periodStart. Subscribing again with the same filter replaces the previous settings. A connection subscribed both to all services and to a specific service gets the specific subscription's settings for that service. Ignored for other topics.
  - `periodStartAt` — number — Services topic only. Start of the stats window in epoch milliseconds, instead of periodMinutes: stats cover everything from this time up to now, for example the start of a shift. It must be on an hour boundary in UTC (stats are kept in hourly UTC buckets, so a start that is not a full UTC hour, such as 08:30, is rejected) and not in the future, otherwise a validation error is returned. The window is exact: windowStartedAt equals this value and periodSeconds is the time since it. It does not slide: the covered span grows until you ask again with a new start. Stats are kept for 24 hours, so a start older than that is clamped to the oldest hour kept (see windowStartedAt for what you got). Cannot be combined with periodMinutes or periodStart. Subscribing again with the same filter replaces the previous settings. Ignored for other topics.
  - `periodStart` — string — Services topic only. Start of the stats window at the start of the current day, instead of periodMinutes. The only value is "today". The window is exact and covers the day up to now, read from hourly buckets; use utcOffsetMinutes to say where the day starts (UTC when omitted). The window start moves to the new day by itself at midnight, so the subscription never needs renewing. Cannot be combined with periodMinutes or periodStartAt. Subscribing again with the same filter replaces the previous settings. Ignored for other topics.
  - `utcOffsetMinutes` — number — Services topic only. With periodStart: offset of the day start from UTC in minutes, for example 120 for UTC+2 or -300 for UTC-5. Must be a whole number of hours between -720 and 840, because stats are kept in hourly UTC buckets; time zones with a half-hour or 45-minute offset are not supported (use periodStartAt there). The offset is fixed for the subscription: subscribe again when daylight saving time changes it. Omit for 0 (UTC day).
  - `serviceLevelSeconds` — number — Services topic only. Service-level target in seconds for answeredWithinSl on the subscribe snapshot and later service_stats_update events. Omit for 20; otherwise one of 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. Subscribing again with the same filter replaces the previous settings. A connection subscribed both to all services and to a specific service gets the specific subscription's settings for that service. Ignored for other topics.
- `WebsocketUnsubscribeAction` — WebsocketUnsubscribeAction
  - `action` — object **(required)**
  - `topic` — string **(required)** _(enum: `conversations`, `transcriptions`, `presence`, `services`)_
  - `filter` — array
    - _array of_ `any`

  - `id` — string — A unique chat channel identifier, distinguish each chat channel across different types.

  - `company` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_

  - `startTime` — number **(required)**
  - `endTime` — number **(required)**
  - `waitTime` — number
  - `duration` — number **(required)**
  - `direction` — string **(required)** _(enum: `INTERNAL`, `INBOUND`, `OUTBOUND`)_
  - `subject` — string
  - `service` — string
  - `serviceTitle` — string
  - `tags` — array
    - _array of_ `ChatTag`
  - `channel` — Channel **(required)**
    - `subject` — string
    - `description` — string
    - `picture` — string — Picture URL
    - `pictureColor` — string — Picture dominant color represented by a hex value.
    - `access` — string _(enum: `private`, `public`)_
    - `company` — string
    - `context` — ChannelContext
      - `source` — string _(enum: `kite`)_
      - `target` — string
      - `events` — array
        - _(nesting depth limit — see `ChannelContextEvent` in the Schemas appendix)_
      - `ptt` — ChannelContextPushToTalk
        - _(nesting depth limit — see `ChannelContextPushToTalk` in the Schemas appendix)_
    - `kite` — boolean
    - `kiteTarget` — string
    - `kiteVariant` — string
    - `kiteAssign` — string
    - `kiteServiceName` — string
    - `kiteDefaultSubject` — string
    - `service` — string
    - `serviceTitle` — string
    - `serviceRecipient` — string
    - `assignee` — User
      - `id` — string **(required)** _(minLen=12; maxLen=12)_
      - `name` — string
      - `email` — string _(pattern=^(^[\w+-]+(\.[\w+-]+)*)@(([\w-]+\.)+\w{2,}$)$)_
      - `phone` — string
      - `picture` — string
      - `locale` — string
      - `timeZone` — string
      - `company` — string
      - `bot` — boolean
      - `pbxDomain` — string
      - `pbxPort` — string
      - `pbxExtension` — string
      - `pbxSerial` — string
      - `pbxUserId` — string
      - `pbxGroupId` — string
      - `createdAt` — string
      - `updatedAt` — string
    - `telephony` — boolean
    - `sms` — boolean
    - `mms` — boolean
    - `whatsapp` — boolean
    - `whatsappStatus` — string _(enum: `24h_channel_closed`)_
    - `messagingChannel` — string — A customer messaging channel that reaches x-bees through classound and is not SMS or WhatsApp. One discriminator instead of a boolean per channel, so a new channel adds a member here and not a set of channel fields. An RCS conversation is not a telephony channel, and its customer id is the person's phone number. _(enum: `messenger`, `instagram`, `rcs`)_
    - `messagingStatus` — string — Set when classound refused a reply because the person's messaging window is closed (a 409 on the send). Unset by the next inbound message, which is the only thing that reopens the window. _(enum: `window_closed`)_
    - `messagingSenderId` — string
    - `messagingReplyUntil` — number
    - `broadcast` — boolean
    - `external` — boolean
    - `autoRecord` — boolean
    - `autoTranscribe` — boolean — Indicates if a conference in the channel starts transcription automatically. When absent, clients follow autoRecord, which used to start both recording and transcription.
    - `transcriptionLanguage` — string
    - `wizyGuestViewOnly` — boolean
    - `channelId` — string **(required)** — Direct-channel ids are the 8-4-4-4-8 slices of the two member ids. An `a_` member id puts `_` in a slice, so the pattern allows it. _(pattern=^[0-9a-z_]{8}\b-[0-9a-z_]{4}\b-[0-9a-z_]{4}\b-[0-9a-z_]{4}\b-[0-9a-z_]{8}$; minLen=32; maxLen=32)_
    - `channelType` — string **(required)** _(enum: `direct`, `group`)_
    - `memberCount` — number **(required)**
    - `createdAt` — string **(required)**
    - `createdBy` — string **(required)**
    - `updatedAt` — string
  - `status` — string _(enum: `WAITFIRSTREPLY`, `WAITREPLYFROMGUEST`, `WAITREPLYFROMAGENT`, `COMPLETED`, `MISSED`)_
  - `participants` — array **(required)**

      - `id` — string **(required)**
      - `info` — ChatParticipantInfo **(required)**
        - _(nesting depth limit — see `ChatParticipantInfo` in the Schemas appendix)_
  - `annotationsStatus` — string _(enum: `AVAILABLE`, `UNAVAILABLE`)_
  - `annotationsByKey` — AnnotationsMap — The newest annotation per `AnnotationKey`: the current value of everything the conversation tracks, without reading the history. Keyed annotations only — a one-off annotation appears solely in `annotations`.
    - _map of_ `Annotation`
      - `id` — string **(required)** — Identity of this emission. Annotations are applied once per id: re-sending one already recorded on the conversation is ignored.
      - `time` — number **(required)**
      - `key` — string — Identity of the value, when the annotation is one reading of something that changes over the conversation. See AnnotationKey. _(pattern=^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]*$; maxLen=100)_
      - `payload` — union **(required)**
        - _(nesting depth limit — see `AnnotationPayload` in the Schemas appendix)_
      - `source` — AnnotationSource **(required)** — Producer of an annotation. Generic identifiers allow callers to attach context such as tool id/name, user id/name, etc., without constraining the source type to a fixed shape.
        - _(nesting depth limit — see `AnnotationSource` in the Schemas appendix)_
  - `type` — string **(required)** _(default=chat)_

  - `requestId` — string
  - `connectionId` — string
  - `message` — string
  - `code` — number
  - `source` — WebsocketSubscribeAction
    - `action` — object **(required)**
    - `topic` — string **(required)** _(enum: `conversations`, `transcriptions`, `presence`, `services`)_
    - `filter` — array
      - _array of_ `any`
    - `state` — boolean
    - `version` — string
    - `stats` — boolean — Services topic only. Opt in to stats: the subscribe snapshot then carries stats and the connection receives service_stats_update events. Stats are also enabled by any of periodMinutes, periodStartAt, periodStart, utcOffsetMinutes or serviceLevelSeconds. Without any of them the subscription gets service and call events only. Ignored for other topics.
    - `buckets` — boolean — Services topic only. Set to true to also get stats.buckets (the stats window as a time series, for trend charts) in the subscribe snapshot and in every service_stats_update. Implies stats. Defaults to false: the series is the largest part of the stats, so it is sent only to the subscriptions that ask for it.
    - `periodMinutes` — number — Services topic only. Rolling lookback window in minutes: omit or 15 for the current 15-minute UTC bucket; 30, 45 or 60 for the last 30, 45 or 60 minutes, read from 15-minute UTC buckets (kept for the last hour only), so the oldest bucket is counted whole and the covered span reported in periodSeconds is up to 15 minutes more. For longer windows use periodStartAt or periodStart. Cannot be combined with periodStartAt or periodStart. Subscribing again with the same filter replaces the previous settings. A connection subscribed both to all services and to a specific service gets the specific subscription's settings for that service. Ignored for other topics.
    - `periodStartAt` — number — Services topic only. Start of the stats window in epoch milliseconds, instead of periodMinutes: stats cover everything from this time up to now, for example the start of a shift. It must be on an hour boundary in UTC (stats are kept in hourly UTC buckets, so a start that is not a full UTC hour, such as 08:30, is rejected) and not in the future, otherwise a validation error is returned. The window is exact: windowStartedAt equals this value and periodSeconds is the time since it. It does not slide: the covered span grows until you ask again with a new start. Stats are kept for 24 hours, so a start older than that is clamped to the oldest hour kept (see windowStartedAt for what you got). Cannot be combined with periodMinutes or periodStart. Subscribing again with the same filter replaces the previous settings. Ignored for other topics.
    - `periodStart` — string — Services topic only. Start of the stats window at the start of the current day, instead of periodMinutes. The only value is "today". The window is exact and covers the day up to now, read from hourly buckets; use utcOffsetMinutes to say where the day starts (UTC when omitted). The window start moves to the new day by itself at midnight, so the subscription never needs renewing. Cannot be combined with periodMinutes or periodStartAt. Subscribing again with the same filter replaces the previous settings. Ignored for other topics.
    - `utcOffsetMinutes` — number — Services topic only. With periodStart: offset of the day start from UTC in minutes, for example 120 for UTC+2 or -300 for UTC-5. Must be a whole number of hours between -720 and 840, because stats are kept in hourly UTC buckets; time zones with a half-hour or 45-minute offset are not supported (use periodStartAt there). The offset is fixed for the subscription: subscribe again when daylight saving time changes it. Omit for 0 (UTC day).
    - `serviceLevelSeconds` — number — Services topic only. Service-level target in seconds for answeredWithinSl on the subscribe snapshot and later service_stats_update events. Omit for 20; otherwise one of 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. Subscribing again with the same filter replaces the previous settings. A connection subscribed both to all services and to a specific service gets the specific subscription's settings for that service. Ignored for other topics.

- `WebhookServiceCallLiveProgressEvent` — WebhookServiceCallLiveProgressEvent
  - `id` — string **(required)**
  - `pbx` — string
  - `company` — string _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
  - `type` — object **(required)**
  - `time` — number **(required)**
  - `integrationId` — string **(required)**
  - `data` — ServiceCallAnalyticsLiveProgressEvent **(required)** — Base service call structure.
    - `id` — string **(required)** — The unique identifier of the service.
    - `pbx` — string **(required)** — The PBX identifier of the service.
    - `time` — number **(required)**
    - `company` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
    - `action` — string _(enum: `INIT`, `WAIT`, `RING`, `REJECT`, `CANCEL`, `ANSWER`, `END`)_
    - `reason` — string — Optional human-readable reason (e.g., 'timeout', 'Normal call clearing').
    - `queuePosition` — number — Queue position captured for this service-call lifecycle step when available.
    - `relatedAgents` — array — Agents related to this action (typically those ringing/answering/cancelling).
      - _array of_ `string`
    - `callId` — string **(required)** — Identifier of the call this record describes.
    - `flowId` — number — Index of a call segment inside one call session. A call can have several flows after CALL.SPLIT (transfer, redirect, etc.)
    - `startTime` — number
    - `direction` — string — Raw direction label for the service call, as the PBX sends it: `incoming` or `outgoing`. Not the CALL-side CallDirection.
    - `customer` — ServiceCustomer
      - `phone` — string **(required)**
      - `name` — string
    - `event` — object **(required)**
    - `eventTrigger` — string **(required)** _(enum: `service.init`, `service.update`, `service.end`, `service.call_init`, `service.call_update`, `service.call_end`, `service.agent_join`, `service.agent_update`, `service.agent_leave`)_
    - `agentsData` — array — Optional agent-specific SIP dialog enrichment for ringing service calls.
      - _array of_ `ServiceCallAgentData`
        - _(nesting depth limit — see `ServiceCallAgentData` in the Schemas appendix)_
    - `timeZone` — string — PBX timeZone (e.g., 'Europe/Kyiv') at the call's start. Set on the SERVICE_CALL_INIT trigger only, and only by PBXs that send it.
    - `aclGroup` — string — ACL group identifier of the service at the call's start. Set on the SERVICE_CALL_INIT trigger only, and only by PBXs that send it.

- `WebhookWhatsAppStatusEvent` — WebhookWhatsAppStatusEvent
  - `id` — string **(required)**
  - `pbx` — string
  - `company` — string _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
  - `type` — object **(required)**
  - `time` — number **(required)**
  - `integrationId` — string **(required)**
  - `data` — WhatsAppStatusEventData **(required)**
    - `from` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3)_
    - `to` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3)_
    - `id` — string **(required)**
    - `status` — string **(required)** — Delivery status of an outbound WhatsApp message in a WHATSAPP.STATUS event. Classound emits QUEUED, SENT, DELIVERED (a provider read report is sent as DELIVERED), DELETED, 24H_CHANNEL_CLOSED and FAILED. ERROR and READ are not emitted by Classound; do not remove them while consumers may still receive them. _(enum: `QUEUED`, `SENT`, `DELIVERED`, `FAILED`, `ERROR`, `READ`, `DELETED`, `24H_CHANNEL_CLOSED`)_
    - `reason` — string **(required)**
    - `channel` — string _(default=whatsapp)_
    - `parts` — number
    - `batchId` — string — Broadcast batch id from the a2s send response; correlates the status back to the originating API call. Absent for non-broadcast messages.
- `WebhookMessengerStatusEvent` — WebhookMessengerStatusEvent — A Facebook Messenger delivery report, delivered to an integration's webhook. The same event the chats queue carries, with the webhook envelope around it: a customer subscribed to delivery reports gets them for SMS, WhatsApp and Messenger alike. Inbound messages have no webhook event on any of the three channels
  - `id` — string **(required)**
  - `pbx` — string
  - `company` — string _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
  - `type` — object **(required)**
  - `time` — number **(required)**
  - `integrationId` — string **(required)**
  - `data` — MessengerStatusConsumeEventData **(required)** — Four differences from the WhatsApp status event this shape was copied from, all four deliberate. Two members are absent. `parts`, because a Messenger message is never segmented the way an SMS is: classound splits a reply into one Messenger message per file plus one for the text, each with its own reference and its own report of its own, so the count a consumer needs is the number of references the send returned and not a number carried on any one report. `batchId`, because nothing broadcasts on this channel: it exists on the WhatsApp event to group the per-recipient statuses of an a2s broadcast, and a Messenger send has one recipient and no batch. Two members are present but declared differently. `reason` is optional here and @required on WhatsApp, because CM.com sends an empty description on a Messenger report often enough that the producer omits the member rather than sending an empty string, and a consumer that only ever reads it on a failure loses nothing. `channel` is an untyped @required String here, where the SMS event has the typed SmsChannelType and the WhatsApp event a `= "whatsapp"` default: this channel has exactly one value, so an enum of one member would carry nothing an enum can carry, and the value is stated by the producer on every event rather than defaulted, so that a consumer never has to decide whether an absent member means messenger or means a producer that forgot
    - `id` — string **(required)** — The reference the send returned in messageIds and MDR holds as supplier_message_id, messenger_<page id>_<uuid4 hex>. A status is matched to the chat message it reports on by this value alone
    - `from` — string **(required)** — The Facebook Page ID the message was sent from, read out of the reference. Not a phone number and never normalised _(minLen=4)_
    - `to` — string **(required)** — The recipient's Page Scoped ID as CM.com reports it. Not a phone number and never normalised _(minLen=4)_
    - `status` — string **(required)** — The final states CM.com reports for a Messenger message, exactly as the producer maps the supplier codes: 1 and 3 are FAILED, 2 is DELIVERED, 4 is READ. Code 0, accepted by the operator, is intermediate and is dropped before the stream, so there is no member for it. The failure is named FAILED and not ERROR, which is what the sibling WhatsApp channel enum calls the same thing: these are the supplier's reports and not a message state, and CM.com's own word for a report of this kind is failed. The consumers translate, kite to MessageMessengerStatus.ERROR and rnc to the red indicator, and the translation is one line in each _(enum: `DELIVERED`, `READ`, `FAILED`)_
    - `reason` — string — CM.com's errorDescription, verbatim. Present on a failure; CM.com also sends one on a success ('Delivered')
    - `channel` — string **(required)** — Always "messenger": the channel stated outright rather than inferred from type
- `WebhookRcsStatusEvent` — WebhookRcsStatusEvent — An RCS delivery report, delivered to an integration's webhook
  - `id` — string **(required)**
  - `pbx` — string
  - `company` — string _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
  - `type` — object **(required)**
  - `time` — number **(required)**
  - `integrationId` — string **(required)**
  - `data` — RcsStatusConsumeEventData **(required)** — Shaped as the Messenger status event, with the same four differences from the WhatsApp one: no `parts`, because each file and the text go out as messages of their own with a reference each; no `batchId`, because nothing broadcasts on this channel; `reason` optional, because CM.com often sends it empty; `channel` an untyped @required String, because the channel has one value and the producer states it on every event
    - `id` — string **(required)** — The reference the send returned in messageIds, rcs_<brand id>_<uuid4 hex>. A status is matched to the chat message it reports on by this value alone
    - `from` — string **(required)** — The brand id the message was sent from, read out of the reference. Not a phone number and never normalised _(minLen=1)_
    - `to` — string **(required)** — The recipient's phone number in E.164 as CM.com reports it, or "unknown" when the report carries none
    - `status` — string **(required)** — The final states CM.com reports for an RCS message, mapped as on Messenger: 1 and 3 are FAILED, 2 is DELIVERED, 4 is READ. Code 0 is intermediate and is dropped before the stream _(enum: `DELIVERED`, `READ`, `FAILED`)_
    - `reason` — string — CM.com's errorDescription, verbatim. Omitted when CM.com sends it empty
    - `channel` — string **(required)** — Always "rcs": the channel stated outright rather than inferred from type
- `ServiceAnalyticsLiveProgressEvent` — ServiceAnalyticsLiveProgressEvent
  - `id` — string **(required)** — The unique identifier of the service.
  - `pbx` — string **(required)** — The PBX identifier of the service.
  - `time` — number **(required)**
  - `company` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
  - `name` — string — The display name of the service.
  - `strategy` — string — Call distribution strategy inside the service (e.g., 'ringall', 'linear', 'rrmemory')
  - `maxCalls` — string
  - `weight` — string — Defines the service priority among other services in terms of call distribution to an agent
  - `timeZone` — string — PBX timeZone (e.g., 'Europe/Kyiv').
  - `aclGroup` — string — ACL group identifier associated with the service.
  - `event` — object **(required)**
  - `eventTrigger` — string **(required)** _(enum: `service.init`, `service.update`, `service.end`, `service.call_init`, `service.call_update`, `service.call_end`, `service.agent_join`, `service.agent_update`, `service.agent_leave`)_
  - `agents` — array — List of agents assigned to the service
    - _array of_ `ServiceAgent`
      - `id` — string **(required)**
      - `penalty` — string
      - `type` — string _(enum: `STATIC`, `DYNAMIC`)_
      - `paused` — boolean
      - `status` — string
      - `reason` — string
      - `message` — string
      - `lastQueueCallEnd` — number
      - `userExtension` — string
      - `userLicense` — string
      - `department` — string
      - `name` — string
      - `aclGroup` — string
      - `statusChangedAt` — number — When the agent's current state began, in epoch milliseconds: the time status, paused or reason last changed. Set by the service on the service events it sends (service.init, service.update, service.agent_join, service.agent_update) and on the services subscribe snapshot; a value sent by the producer is ignored. A service.init that repeats an agent's state keeps the earlier time, so the timer survives a PBX resync; the end of a queue call does not change it.
  - `calls` — array — List of calls in the service
    - _array of_ `string`
  - `stats` — ServiceStats — Lookback volume and agent counters for overlapping 15-minute UTC buckets. Default lookback is the current 15-minute UTC bucket when periodMinutes is omitted or 15. Live queue depth and derived rates/averages are computed by the client. Counters are updated as calls progress: offered and waitCount when a call enters the queue; answered, answeredWaitSumMs, maxWaitMs and the service-level histogram when it is answered; every other counter (including unanswered, abandoned, durations and per-agent counters) only when the call completes.
    - `offered` — number — Number of queue calls offered in the requested lookback window: every call that entered the queue, counted when it enters. Per-agent offered counts the calls rung to that agent.
    - `outbound` — number — Number of outbound queue calls received in the requested lookback window.
    - `answered` — number — Number of calls answered in the requested lookback window. Counted when the call is answered.
    - `unanswered` — number — Number of unanswered queue calls in the requested lookback window.
    - `unknown` — number — Number of queue calls in the requested lookback window that ended without an outcome: nobody answered and the call never reported an end (it was closed after going silent). With no call waiting, offered = (answered - transferred) + transferred + abandoned + unanswered + unknown, where answered includes the transferred calls.
    - `abandoned` — number — Number of queue-abandoned calls (caller hung up without an answer) in the requested lookback window, including the short abandons counted in shortAbandoned.
    - `shortAbandoned` — number — Number of short-abandoned calls (caller hung up within 5s without an answer) in the requested lookback window. A part of abandoned, not in addition to it.
    - `transferred` — number — Number of answered queue calls in the requested lookback window that an agent passed on: the call ended with a transfer or a forward (reason of the call end). A call nobody answered is never counted here.
    - `answeredWaitSumMs` — number — Total wait time in milliseconds of answered calls in the requested lookback window, added when the call is answered. Divide by answered for the average speed of answer (ASA).
    - `abandonedWaitSumMs` — number — Total wait time in milliseconds of abandoned calls (the caller hung up before an answer) in the requested lookback window, added when the call completes.
    - `unansweredWaitSumMs` — number — Total wait time in milliseconds of calls that ended without an answer and were not abandoned (for example a queue timeout, or an unknown outcome) in the requested lookback window, added when the call completes.
    - `waitCount` — number — Number of queue waits in the requested lookback window, counted when the call enters the queue. Until a call is answered or completes its wait is not yet in the wait sums, so (answeredWaitSumMs + abandonedWaitSumMs + unansweredWaitSumMs) / waitCount understates the average while calls are waiting.
    - `talkSumMs` — number — Total talk duration in milliseconds for answered calls in the requested lookback window.
    - `talkCount` — number — Number of answered calls included in talkSumMs in the requested lookback window.
    - `acwSumMs` — number — Total after-call work time in milliseconds in the requested lookback window. Time agents spent in wrap-up (agent update reason 'Wrap-up time'), added when the interval ends, so an agent still in wrap-up is not included yet.
    - `ringSumMs` — number — Total ring time in milliseconds of the service's calls in the requested lookback window, added when each call completes. Per call: from the first time the call started ringing any agent to the answer, or to the end of the call when nobody answered; re-rings and pauses included.
    - `ringCount` — number — Number of calls included in ringSumMs in the requested lookback window. Calls that never rang an agent are not counted.
    - `answeredWithinSl` — number — Number of calls answered within serviceLevelSeconds in the requested lookback window. Service level is the numerator answeredWithinSl divided by the calls with a known outcome, short abandons (likely misdials) left out: answered + (abandoned - shortAbandoned) + unanswered, where abandoned includes shortAbandoned. Calls still waiting are not in the base.
    - `serviceLevelSeconds` — number — Service-level target in seconds that answeredWithinSl was counted against. 20 when the request omitted serviceLevelSeconds.
    - `maxWaitMs` — number — Maximum queue wait time in milliseconds among waits that have ended in the requested lookback window (set when a call is answered, or when it ends unanswered). Calls still waiting are not included; see longestWaitStartedAt.
    - `windowStartedAt` — number — Start of the requested lookback window in epoch milliseconds (oldest overlapping 15-minute UTC bucket).
    - `longestWaitStartedAt` — number — Point-in-time, independent of periodMinutes: start time (when the call entered the queue) of the longest-waiting call that is still in the queue at asOf, in epoch milliseconds. Omitted when no call is waiting. Clients derive the longest wait time (LWT) as now - longestWaitStartedAt and tick it locally between events. Unlike maxWaitMs it excludes calls whose wait has already ended.
    - `callsWaiting` — number — Point-in-time, independent of periodMinutes: number of calls that are in the queue at asOf and not yet answered (last action INIT, WAIT, RING or REJECT). 0 when nobody is waiting. Clients keep it current between events from the service call events.
    - `callsActive` — number — Point-in-time, independent of periodMinutes: number of calls answered by an agent and not yet ended at asOf (last action ANSWER). 0 when nobody is talking. Clients keep it current between events from the service call events.
    - `agentsTotal` — number — Point-in-time, independent of periodMinutes: number of agents of the service at asOf. Only business and premium licensed agents are counted, like in agentStats. Equals agentsAvailable + agentsTalking + agentsPaused + agentsWrapUp + agentsLoggedOff.
    - `agentsAvailable` — number — Point-in-time: agents that are logged in, not paused and not on a call (status available, idle or ready).
    - `agentsTalking` — number — Point-in-time: agents on a call, that is agents related to a service call whose last action is ANSWER, or whose status says they are busy (busy, inuse, in_use, talking, ringing).
    - `agentsPaused` — number — Point-in-time: agents that are paused (paused flag, or status pause, paused or break) and not in wrap-up.
    - `agentsWrapUp` — number — Point-in-time: agents in wrap-up (after call work), that is paused with the reason 'Wrap-up time', the same signal that is counted in acwSumMs.
    - `agentsLoggedOff` — number — Point-in-time: agents that are logged off or unavailable: status offline, unavailable, loggedoff, logged_off, logged-out, logout or unregistered, and any status that is not one of the known available, busy, paused or wrap-up statuses.
    - `asOf` — number — When these stats were last refreshed, in epoch milliseconds.
    - `periodSeconds` — number — Seconds from windowStartedAt to the time the stats were read. Counters include every overlapping 15-minute UTC bucket in full, so this can exceed the nominal periodMinutes by up to one bucket (just under 900 seconds, or just under 3600 for lookbacks of 2 hours and longer). For the default current bucket it is the seconds elapsed since that bucket started, below 900.

    - `bucketSeconds` — number — Width of each item of buckets in seconds: 900 for lookbacks of up to 60 minutes (15-minute UTC buckets), 3600 for windows from a start (periodStartAt, periodStart), which are read from hourly UTC buckets. Present with buckets.
    - `buckets` — array — The window as a time series, only when asked for (the buckets subscribe option, includeBuckets of GetServiceStats): one item per stored bucket the window overlaps, oldest first, from windowStartedAt up to the bucket that holds asOf, which is still filling; a bucket without calls is sent with zero counters. A window from a start is at most 24 items (25 when a periodStartAt older than 24 hours is clamped). Raw counters, never rates or averages, so the buckets of several services can be summed; each counter of the window equals the sum of its buckets (maxWaitMs: the greatest). A counter lands in the bucket of the moment it is counted (see ServiceStats): a call that entered the queue at 09:58 and was answered at 10:01 is offered in the 09:00 bucket and answered in the 10:00 one.

- `ServiceStatsSnapshotEvent` — ServiceStatsSnapshotEvent — Snapshot of the service stats state, produced after service call and agent events, at most once per 5 seconds per service. Carries only the periods changed since the previous snapshot (15-minute and hourly), with absolute values, and the open occupancy interval of every known agent. Hourly periods are sent at most once per minute. At every 15-minute UTC bucket boundary a service that was active within the last 24 hours also gets a snapshot, so subscribers can move their lookback windows on; it repeats the period that just closed with all its agents.

  - `pbx` — string **(required)** — The PBX identifier of the service.
  - `time` — number **(required)**
  - `company` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
  - `event` — object **(required)**
  - `version` — number **(required)** — Grows with every snapshot of a service.
  - `sentAt` — number **(required)** — Time (epoch ms) the snapshot was produced at.
  - `periods` — array **(required)** — Periods changed since the previous snapshot.
    - _array of_ `ServiceStatsPeriodSnapshot`
      - `windowStartedAt` — number **(required)** — Start of the 15-minute UTC period (epoch ms).
      - `offered` — number — Number of queue calls offered in the period: every call that entered the queue, counted when it enters.
      - `outbound` — number — Number of outbound queue calls received in the period.
      - `answered` — number — Number of calls answered in the period.
      - `unanswered` — number — Number of unanswered queue calls in the period.
      - `unknown` — number — Number of queue calls that ended without an outcome: nobody answered and the call never reported an end (it was closed after going silent).
      - `abandoned` — number — Number of queue-abandoned calls (caller hung up without an answer), including the short abandons counted in shortAbandoned.
      - `shortAbandoned` — number — Number of short-abandoned calls (caller hung up within 5s without an answer). A part of abandoned, not in addition to it.
      - `transferred` — number — Number of answered queue calls that an agent passed on: the call ended with a transfer or a forward (reason of the call end). A call nobody answered is never counted here.

      - `abandonedWaitSumMs` — number — Total wait time in milliseconds of abandoned calls.
      - `unansweredWaitSumMs` — number — Total wait time in milliseconds of calls that ended without an answer and were not abandoned.
      - `waitCount` — number — Number of queue waits, counted when the call enters the queue.
      - `talkSumMs` — number — Total talk duration in milliseconds of answered calls.
      - `talkCount` — number — Number of answered calls included in talkSumMs.
      - `acwSumMs` — number — Total after-call work time in milliseconds. Time agents spent in wrap-up (agent update reason 'Wrap-up time'), added when the interval ends, so an agent still in wrap-up is not included yet.
      - `ringSumMs` — number — Total ring time in milliseconds of calls whose ring has ended, from the first ring of any agent to the answer or, when nobody answered, to the end of the call.
      - `ringCount` — number — Number of calls included in ringSumMs.
      - `maxWaitMs` — number — Maximum queue wait time in milliseconds among waits that have ended.
      - `waitBucket5s` — number — Answered calls that waited up to 5 seconds.
      - `waitBucket10s` — number — Answered calls that waited more than 5 and up to 10 seconds.
      - `waitBucket15s` — number — Answered calls that waited more than 10 and up to 15 seconds.
      - `waitBucket20s` — number — Answered calls that waited more than 15 and up to 20 seconds.
      - `waitBucket25s` — number — Answered calls that waited more than 20 and up to 25 seconds.
      - `waitBucket30s` — number — Answered calls that waited more than 25 and up to 30 seconds.
      - `waitBucketGt30s` — number — Answered calls that waited more than 30 seconds.
      - `agents` — array — Absolute per-agent counters of the period, only for the agents whose counters changed since the previous snapshot; the others are already stored. A period that has just closed is sent once more with all its agents.

- `ServiceStatsAnalyticsLiveEvent` — ServiceStatsAnalyticsLiveEvent
  - `id` — string **(required)** — The unique identifier of the service.
  - `pbx` — string **(required)** — The PBX identifier of the service.
  - `time` — number **(required)**
  - `company` — string **(required)** _(minLen=3; maxLen=30)_
  - `event` — object **(required)**
  - `version` — number **(required)** — Version of the stats snapshot that triggered this event. Grows with every snapshot of a service; a client ignores an event older than the one it already applied.
  - `stats` — ServiceStats **(required)** — Lookback volume and agent counters for overlapping 15-minute UTC buckets. Default lookback is the current 15-minute UTC bucket when periodMinutes is omitted or 15. Live queue depth and derived rates/averages are computed by the client. Counters are updated as calls progress: offered and waitCount when a call enters the queue; answered, answeredWaitSumMs, maxWaitMs and the service-level histogram when it is answered; every other counter (including unanswered, abandoned, durations and per-agent counters) only when the call completes.
    - `offered` — number — Number of queue calls offered in the requested lookback window: every call that entered the queue, counted when it enters. Per-agent offered counts the calls rung to that agent.
    - `outbound` — number — Number of outbound queue calls received in the requested lookback window.
    - `answered` — number — Number of calls answered in the requested lookback window. Counted when the call is answered.
    - `unanswered` — number — Number of unanswered queue calls in the requested lookback window.
    - `unknown` — number — Number of queue calls in the requested lookback window that ended without an outcome: nobody answered and the call never reported an end (it was closed after going silent). With no call waiting, offered = (answered - transferred) + transferred + abandoned + unanswered + unknown, where answered includes the transferred calls.
    - `abandoned` — number — Number of queue-abandoned calls (caller hung up without an answer) in the requested lookback window, including the short abandons counted in shortAbandoned.
    - `shortAbandoned` — number — Number of short-abandoned calls (caller hung up within 5s without an answer) in the requested lookback window. A part of abandoned, not in addition to it.
    - `transferred` — number — Number of answered queue calls in the requested lookback window that an agent passed on: the call ended with a transfer or a forward (reason of the call end). A call nobody answered is never counted here.
    - `answeredWaitSumMs` — number — Total wait time in milliseconds of answered calls in the requested lookback window, added when the call is answered. Divide by answered for the average speed of answer (ASA).
    - `abandonedWaitSumMs` — number — Total wait time in milliseconds of abandoned calls (the caller hung up before an answer) in the requested lookback window, added when the call completes.
    - `unansweredWaitSumMs` — number — Total wait time in milliseconds of calls that ended without an answer and were not abandoned (for example a queue timeout, or an unknown outcome) in the requested lookback window, added when the call completes.
    - `waitCount` — number — Number of queue waits in the requested lookback window, counted when the call enters the queue. Until a call is answered or completes its wait is not yet in the wait sums, so (answeredWaitSumMs + abandonedWaitSumMs + unansweredWaitSumMs) / waitCount understates the average while calls are waiting.
    - `talkSumMs` — number — Total talk duration in milliseconds for answered calls in the requested lookback window.
    - `talkCount` — number — Number of answered calls included in talkSumMs in the requested lookback window.
    - `acwSumMs` — number — Total after-call work time in milliseconds in the requested lookback window. Time agents spent in wrap-up (agent update reason 'Wrap-up time'), added when the interval ends, so an agent still in wrap-up is not included yet.
    - `ringSumMs` — number — Total ring time in milliseconds of the service's calls in the requested lookback window, added when each call completes. Per call: from the first time the call started ringing any agent to the answer, or to the end of the call when nobody answered; re-rings and pauses included.
    - `ringCount` — number — Number of calls included in ringSumMs in the requested lookback window. Calls that never rang an agent are not counted.
    - `answeredWithinSl` — number — Number of calls answered within serviceLevelSeconds in the requested lookback window. Service level is the numerator answeredWithinSl divided by the calls with a known outcome, short abandons (likely misdials) left out: answered + (abandoned - shortAbandoned) + unanswered, where abandoned includes shortAbandoned. Calls still waiting are not in the base.
    - `serviceLevelSeconds` — number — Service-level target in seconds that answeredWithinSl was counted against. 20 when the request omitted serviceLevelSeconds.
    - `maxWaitMs` — number — Maximum queue wait time in milliseconds among waits that have ended in the requested lookback window (set when a call is answered, or when it ends unanswered). Calls still waiting are not included; see longestWaitStartedAt.
    - `windowStartedAt` — number — Start of the requested lookback window in epoch milliseconds (oldest overlapping 15-minute UTC bucket).
    - `longestWaitStartedAt` — number — Point-in-time, independent of periodMinutes: start time (when the call entered the queue) of the longest-waiting call that is still in the queue at asOf, in epoch milliseconds. Omitted when no call is waiting. Clients derive the longest wait time (LWT) as now - longestWaitStartedAt and tick it locally between events. Unlike maxWaitMs it excludes calls whose wait has already ended.
    - `callsWaiting` — number — Point-in-time, independent of periodMinutes: number of calls that are in the queue at asOf and not yet answered (last action INIT, WAIT, RING or REJECT). 0 when nobody is waiting. Clients keep it current between events from the service call events.
    - `callsActive` — number — Point-in-time, independent of periodMinutes: number of calls answered by an agent and not yet ended at asOf (last action ANSWER). 0 when nobody is talking. Clients keep it current between events from the service call events.
    - `agentsTotal` — number — Point-in-time, independent of periodMinutes: number of agents of the service at asOf. Only business and premium licensed agents are counted, like in agentStats. Equals agentsAvailable + agentsTalking + agentsPaused + agentsWrapUp + agentsLoggedOff.
    - `agentsAvailable` — number — Point-in-time: agents that are logged in, not paused and not on a call (status available, idle or ready).
    - `agentsTalking` — number — Point-in-time: agents on a call, that is agents related to a service call whose last action is ANSWER, or whose status says they are busy (busy, inuse, in_use, talking, ringing).
    - `agentsPaused` — number — Point-in-time: agents that are paused (paused flag, or status pause, paused or break) and not in wrap-up.
    - `agentsWrapUp` — number — Point-in-time: agents in wrap-up (after call work), that is paused with the reason 'Wrap-up time', the same signal that is counted in acwSumMs.
    - `agentsLoggedOff` — number — Point-in-time: agents that are logged off or unavailable: status offline, unavailable, loggedoff, logged_off, logged-out, logout or unregistered, and any status that is not one of the known available, busy, paused or wrap-up statuses.
    - `asOf` — number — When these stats were last refreshed, in epoch milliseconds.
    - `periodSeconds` — number — Seconds from windowStartedAt to the time the stats were read. Counters include every overlapping 15-minute UTC bucket in full, so this can exceed the nominal periodMinutes by up to one bucket (just under 900 seconds, or just under 3600 for lookbacks of 2 hours and longer). For the default current bucket it is the seconds elapsed since that bucket started, below 900.
    - `agentStats` — ServiceAgentStatsMap
      - _map of_ `ServiceAgentStats`
        - _(nesting depth limit — see `ServiceAgentStats` in the Schemas appendix)_
    - `bucketSeconds` — number — Width of each item of buckets in seconds: 900 for lookbacks of up to 60 minutes (15-minute UTC buckets), 3600 for windows from a start (periodStartAt, periodStart), which are read from hourly UTC buckets. Present with buckets.
    - `buckets` — array — The window as a time series, only when asked for (the buckets subscribe option, includeBuckets of GetServiceStats): one item per stored bucket the window overlaps, oldest first, from windowStartedAt up to the bucket that holds asOf, which is still filling; a bucket without calls is sent with zero counters. A window from a start is at most 24 items (25 when a periodStartAt older than 24 hours is clamped). Raw counters, never rates or averages, so the buckets of several services can be summed; each counter of the window equals the sum of its buckets (maxWaitMs: the greatest). A counter lands in the bucket of the moment it is counted (see ServiceStats): a call that entered the queue at 09:58 and was answered at 10:01 is offered in the 09:00 bucket and answered in the 10:00 one.
      - _array of_ `ServiceStatsBucket`
        - _(nesting depth limit — see `ServiceStatsBucket` in the Schemas appendix)_

        - _oneOf_ — exactly one of:
          - **`button`**
            - _(nesting depth limit — inline object, see the parent schema in the Schemas appendix)_
  - **`wilma`**
    - `wilma` — WilmaChatElement **(required)** — On every agent reply of a Wilma chat on the stream transport: the session and turn that produced it, how the turn went and what it shared. `verbosity` is the agent's setting when the session started; clients decide from it what to show. The turn's events are `startIndex`..`endIndex` of the session log: read them with GetSessionEvents(sessionId, startIndex).
      - `sessionId` — string **(required)** _(minLen=1; maxLen=64)_
      - `verbosity` — string **(required)** — How much of a chat turn x-bees shows while the agent works. SMS and WhatsApp always send one final text. _(enum: `none`, `simple`, `full`)_
      - `turn` — number **(required)** — The turn of the session that produced this message. A steer that joins a running turn shares it. _(min=1)_
      - `startIndex` — number **(required)** — Index of the turn's first event (`turnStarted`) in the session log. _(min=0)_
      - `endIndex` — number — Index of the turn's last event (completed, failed or stopped). Absent when the message was written before the turn ended. _(min=0)_
      - `summary` — WilmaChatTurnSummary **(required)** — How the turn went. The calls themselves (input, output) are not stored here: they are the turn's events in the session log.
        - `outcome` — string **(required)** — How the turn ended. _(enum: `done`, `stopped`, `failed`)_
        - `durationMs` — number — From the turn's start to its end. Absent when the turn had not ended.
        - `toolCount` — number **(required)** — Steps the turn took, counted as the Wilma assistant counts its work steps: each tool call and each sandbox step (`SandboxStartedEvent`, `SandboxFailedEvent`).
        - `failedCount` — number **(required)** — Steps that failed: calls that failed, including those the stop or failure cut off, and sandbox steps that failed.
      - `artifacts` — array
        - _array of_ `WilmaChatArtifact`
          - _(nesting depth limit — see `WilmaChatArtifact` in the Schemas appendix)_
